title: Dreams of a better world
summary: Whether scattered hunters can ever change the world.

claims.text: Most imbued barely grasp the world they woke to, and many go mad or die trying; the scattered few barely ripple a sea of supernatural beings, so their wins leave the wider world mostly unchanged.
Human apathy and disbelief, the weight of supernatural influence and the creatures' own efforts to crush resistance all keep hunters' discoveries unheard.
Small successive victories, or a little common ground found with monsters, can give some hunters hope of a better life for family, friends or a neighbourhood.

Reaching for more means coming out of hiding to link up with hunters elsewhere, which draws the eye of mortal authorities and powerful monsters and risks being condemned by a public blinded by monstrous lies.
Calling the hunt a grassroots movement would overstate it; it has almost no coordinated direction.
